references.text: Refers to God's care for those who fear him and keep his covenant, parallel to doing God's will in Matthew 12:50.
God values those who are humble and tremble at his word, which is similar to doing his will as mentioned in Matthew 12:50.
Emphasizes the importance of doing God's will to enter the kingdom of heaven, consistent with the message in Matthew 12:50.
Mark repeats a similar theme to Matthew 12:50 about being Jesus' spiritual family by doing God's will.
Luke also highlights the significance of hearing God's word and following it, parallel to doing God's will in Matthew 12:50.
Focuses on the importance of becoming perfect through doing God's will, which resonates with the message in Matthew 12:50.
John speaks about loving not only with words but with actions and truth, which can be seen as part of doing God's will as in Matthew 12:50.
